newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close down after rain.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close down after rain.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed down on Sunday after rains that are expected to kill a White Fly pest in the main growing Punjab province, brokers said.

"The rains will lessen the impact of the pest attack on the cotton crop in Punjab," broker Nasim Usman at Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said. "Rain usually kills the White Fly, which sucks juice from the cotton plant and makes it weaker."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,150 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) compared to Saturday's 2,175.
The rates were likely to open lower on Monday, Usman said.
